newsitem.title: UK: Greycoat says Moorfield still silent.
newsitem.headline: Greycoat says Moorfield still silent.

text.p: British property company Greycoat Plc, in the midst of an assault by rebel shareholders aimed at splitting up the group and divesting some of its assets, said on Friday it had yet to receive any detailed proposals from Moorfield Estates Plc, which claims to have a merger plan.
An extraordinary shareholders meeting to vote on a resolution to change Greycoat is due to reconvene at noon on December 5, at the Bakers' Hall in London.
An original meeting on November 14 was adjourned for three weeks with the aim of allowing the Greycoat board to consider Moorfield's draft proposals in detail, once they were in hand.

"To date we have not received any further information from Moorfield even though over a week ago your company asked Moorfield to supply full details which we would consider carefully," the board said in a statement to shareholders.

"Your board continues to consider that it is very important and in the best interests of shareholders as a whole that you vote against the resolution. Inaction on your part could result in the resolution being passed by default," Greycoat added.
